What the Hell happened to Black Canary?

When I was growing up in the 90s, Wonder Woman went out of spotlight for awhile. I didn't catch that wave. Being a little girl, I wasn't allowed to have comic books, but I loved Batman. I loved Batgirl. The Animated series was the first memories I had. Then, when I was 11, all of a sudden Justice League came out. I got to see real heroines in action. Wonder Woman. Hawk Girl. Oh my god, was this awesome for me. I didn't have to want to be like a guy anymore. Hawk Girl was smart, angry, bold, a warrior and she was perfect. The series led me to Green Arrow, my favorite superhero.

Black Canary. That's a bitch who can get shit DONE. Trained by Ted Grant -- one of the sexiest older heroes in history--- and completely independent, falls in love with green arrow. She was wicked sharp, wicked sexy, and someone who I could aspire to be like.

Not anymore. Now DC has taken her back to the fucking 70s and early 80s.

"You know what would be cool? If she was the singer of a band and fought crime!" Okay Josie and the Pussycats/Jem and the Holograms/Jabberjaw. Hold your fucking horses. This isn't okay.

I'm all for trying to get teenaged girls into comics. I've been into comics since I could check them out from my library ( 2001, Same year justice league came out). Let me tell you this.... those stories were fucking compelling. They made me cope with these ideas:

Yes, I am a girl, and it doesn't make me any less weak. It's okay to not like pink. It's okay to be badass. it's okay to fight if what you're fighting for is in the right place. It's okay to be female, as long as you realize you're not a secondary area that people pander to. It's okay to love science and kicking ass.

Now, I look at Batgirl and I look at Black Canary and It's like they're getting the wrong message across. Look at Flash. Look at green arrow. Their stories are complex, well written, and so action packed without that awkward foot setting. Look at the comics. Look at the female characters. look at their feet. Do they stand confidently? No. I only see the "awkward foot shuffle." and the fact that batgirl talks about split ends when she's in the middle of a hunt.

That's not okay with me. You know what'd I'd say when I'm in the middle of a video game filled world?

"This is really pushing my buttons."

Lighthearted. Funny. whatever. No. Wonder Woman gets to be strong, but what about the rest of them? I'm angry.

I never got the chance to see a strong heroine when I was a kid until I was 11. It's not okay with me that they're just... doing this. I'm not okay with it, and I'm a far cry from feminist. I believe in equality. So please, DC, let Dinah Lance be Badass again, without appealing to what you thing a majority of pop culture wants the teenaged girls to be.

Because if DC lets that happen.... well.... then I wouldn't be who I am today. I Would care more about appearance than a thought filled person. No.

Let barbara and dinah be strong. Let them be strong and away from cliches and give a new generation of girls something to look up to. Because I never had it.

Growing up, you were either smart or pretty. Never both. When I was in my teenaged years, suddenly these two appeared. Gorgeous and smart, and very much an equal to their male counterparts. I know It sounds preachy, I'm sorry. But when you think of your sisters or daughters, would you rather them look up to a hero, or a pop culture reference?

I'm so sickened of looking at heroines and seeing them reduced to something that is just.... less than sub par. Girls don't want a pop culture reference. We want to feel like we are part of the man's world of heroes. I wasn't special. I wanted to fit in. I am female, yes, but I believe that everyone deserves a story that is equally awesome.

While I am not very familiar with Black Canary, I understand where you are coming from and I completely agree. I have always been a fan of strong female characters and I don't see any reason to "prettify" them for mainstream consumption. You mentioned one of my favorites, Wonder Woman.

Talk about an amazing role model, she was always the epitome of what a strong woman could be. Hell, she could even trade punches with Superman if push came to shove. There was never a question in your mind that you were required to take her seriously.

We need more female heroes we can take seriously. They can be positive role models while remaining absolute badasses at the same time.

I agree. The only issue I have with badass female characters is that they are reduced to some sort of a killing machine that is so much better than the men around, but at the same time making it a very flat and boring character cutout. I think what we need to see more are badass female characters who are also very human, and through that humanity to teach and inspire people of all ages.

Just my two cents.
Absolutely, character depth is paramount. We need humanity to be able to relate to them.
I agree. Batgirl/Oracle was a good example of a well written and diverse psychological character...until the recent comic line.

It's so surreal how different the meaning of "socialist" is in the US and in Europe. That is, the perceived meaning in the heads of the people, not the text book definitions.

In the US, we spent most of the 20th century fighting, dying, or in a Mutually Assured Destruction stalemate against one form of socialist or another. Those cuts run deep. When we see some of our former enemies making strategic alliances against us, as China and Russia currently are doing as well as de-valuing our monetary system, then we change our threat posture against all perceived collaborators, sympathizers, and subversives. Using the general term of socialist or Marxist is an effective way to corral all three categories into a single unified threat.

Also, the text book definition of socialism is naive. For at least the last 2000 years (probably longer), there have been countless attempts at communal social organization that fits the "Socialist" textbook definition. All those failed attempts have shown that communal organization cannot scale above the tribal, city, or kibbutz level. Meanwhile, Capitalism cannot scale down once it crosses a certain threshold of productivity. Most of the last 5 centuries have been attempts to find a happy balance between those two extremes- most have failed from figuring out how to pay for social programs, impose effective economic moral hazard against the top classes, or at how to incentive productivity and compassion at all levels of society.

This is misleading. Their power grid was ruled to be fine, and the linked article also conflate all accusations with the realities. When this dropped in 2013 it was the same shit. In reality, the ruling is that they have to hook up to water and sewage, even if they don't use it. The reason for this is legislation written before the idea of composting toilets and effective rainwater catch systems. The fight is with the specific code, and the judge made the right call to point this out. The code is designed to keep water a monopoly, when rainwater catch would benefit many people and pull volume out of the water pumping system. If that happens the monopoly company could lose substantially and have to raise rates a lot. The code is bizarre, but this ruling is not an antihomesteading stand. \
